memory_candidates.content: In guard-destructive-git.sh-style bash detectors that must inspect individual command tokens, never iterate with unquoted word-splitting (`for tok in $seg_rest`) -- the shell's own pathname expansion can silently consume a literal glob token (e.g. `src/*.lean`) before the detector's own glob-metacharacter check ever sees it, if matching files happen to exist in cwd. Use `read -ra arr <<< "$seg_rest"` then iterate `"${arr[@]}"` instead -- this splits on IFS whitespace without triggering pathname expansion.

Several source-store verification scripts (generate-context-line-counts.sh, validate-context-index.sh, and others sharing deploy-root-guard.sh) refuse to run when invoked directly from agent-system/extensions/<ext>/scripts/ because their relative '../..' path resolution assumes a deployed tree. They document a deliberate bypass: prefix the invocation with `REPO_ROOT=$(pwd)` (repo root) to run them against the source store directly, without needing a prior redeploy. Useful when a plan phase needs a source-store-side check before Phase 4's redeploy.
